nextjs.recommended_path: Railway service with Nixpacks builder. Set start command to `npm run start` after build. Use `${{ Postgres.DATABASE_URL }}` reference for any DB.
caveats: Static-only Next.js (export) is wasted on Railway — point at Vercel/Netlify/Pages instead.
Image optimization needs `sharp`; Nixpacks installs it automatically.
ISR / on-demand revalidation: confirm route segment configuration; Railway runs a long-lived Node process so all data-fetching modes are supported.

astro.recommended_path: Server / hybrid Astro is fine on Railway via the Node adapter. Static-only Astro is better off on Pages/Netlify.
caveats: If output is purely static, Railway is the wrong host — no edge cache benefits.
Use `@astrojs/node` adapter; set startCommand to `node ./dist/server/entry.mjs`.

sveltekit.recommended_path: Railway with `@sveltejs/adapter-node`. Set startCommand to `node build`.
caveats: Use HOST=0.0.0.0 in env (Railway provides PORT).

remix.recommended_path: Railway with the Remix Node template. `npm run start` after build.
caveats: Loaders/actions are long-lived Node — no edge-runtime constraints.

nuxt.recommended_path: Railway with Nitro Node preset. `node .output/server/index.mjs` after `nuxt build`.

express.recommended_path: Railway is express's natural home. Nixpacks detects, builds, runs `node` against your start script.
caveats: Bind to 0.0.0.0:$PORT — Railway sets PORT in env.
express-session in-memory: stays in-memory per replica. Use Redis (add a Redis service) when you scale to >1 replica.
dependencies_to_flag: multer (disk uploads — use volume or shift to R2)

fastify.recommended_path: Same as Express. Nixpacks detects + runs.

nestjs.recommended_path: Railway runs NestJS without modification. Build via `npm run build`, run `node dist/main`. TypeORM and the full DI stack are supported.
caveats: Microservices via TCP transport require service-to-service private networking — use Railway private networking via service domains.

hono.recommended_path: Hono on Node adapter runs fine on Railway. If you want the edge-runtime experience, point at Cloudflare Workers instead.

rails.recommended_path: Railway is one of the cleanest Rails homes after Heroku-style platforms. Nixpacks detects Gemfile.lock, runs `bundle install`, `rails server -b 0.0.0.0`. Sidekiq workers run as a second service.
caveats: ActionCable WebSockets work over Railway's HTTPS endpoint — confirm your client uses wss:// to the public domain.
ActiveStorage on local disk requires a volume; better path is S3-compatible (R2/S3) backend.

django.recommended_path: Nixpacks detects requirements.txt. `gunicorn <project>.wsgi --bind 0.0.0.0:$PORT --workers <N>`. Celery workers as a second service.
caveats: Channels (WebSockets/ASGI) — switch to `daphne` or `uvicorn` and serve via the same public domain.
Static files: collectstatic + serve via WhiteNoise OR ship to R2/S3.

flask.recommended_path: Railway runs Flask via gunicorn just like Django. `gunicorn app:app --bind 0.0.0.0:$PORT`.

spring-boot.recommended_path: Railway via Nixpacks Java provider or Dockerfile. Spring Boot's embedded server binds to $PORT.
caveats: JVM cold-start matters at low traffic — consider always-on (no sleep) for production.

dotnet.recommended_path: Railway runs ASP.NET via Nixpacks .NET provider or Dockerfile. Bind to ASPNETCORE_URLS=http://0.0.0.0:$PORT.

go-monolith.recommended_path: Nixpacks detects go.mod. Builds + runs the resulting binary. Tiny container, fast cold-start.

rust.recommended_path: Nixpacks detects Cargo.toml. Builds release binary, runs it.
caveats: Build time can be slow — use a Dockerfile with `cargo chef` for caching if iteration speed matters.

deno.recommended_path: Nixpacks supports Deno. Use `deno task start` or `deno run --allow-all main.ts`.

bun.recommended_path: Nixpacks supports Bun. `bun run start` is the canonical entry.

elixir.recommended_path: Phoenix / OTP apps run well on Railway. Nixpacks builds via `mix release`. Cluster across services using libcluster + private networking.
caveats: Distillery / multi-node clustering: Railway's private networking provides per-service DNS; configure `node_basename` accordingly.
Long-lived Phoenix Channels (WebSockets) supported on the public HTTPS endpoint.

crystal.recommended_path: Nixpacks supports Crystal. `crystal build src/main.cr --release`, run binary.

wordpress.recommended_path: WordPress + MySQL works on Railway via Dockerfile. But Railway is not WordPress-focused — managed WP hosts (Kinsta, WP Engine) ship more guardrails.
caveats: wp-content uploads need a volume (Railway volume) or S3-compatible offload.
wp-cron under load: disable wp_cron and run a Railway cron service.

laravel.recommended_path: Railway runs PHP-FPM via Nixpacks PHP provider or Dockerfile. `php artisan serve` for dev, nginx + php-fpm for prod.
caveats: Queue workers as a separate service.
Schedule via the Railway cron service kind.

static-html.recommended_path: Don't host static sites on Railway — you pay for a long-lived process to serve files. Use Cloudflare Pages, Netlify, or Vercel for static.

hugo.recommended_path: Hugo's output is static — Pages/Netlify/Vercel are the right hosts. Railway is paying for compute you don't need.

jekyll.recommended_path: Same as Hugo. Static output → static host.

vite-spa.recommended_path: Vite-built SPA is static — point at a static host (Pages/Netlify/Vercel).

static.recommended_path: Static sites belong on a static host. Railway is a compute platform.

media-processing-heavy.recommended_path: Railway can run FFmpeg / sharp / ImageMagick services, but you pay $/vCPU-h for the process. Heavy batch jobs are cheaper on serverless (Lambda / Cloud Run) or Containers.
caveats: Volume IO matters — persistent volumes are local NVMe but bandwidth-priced.
Headless browsers work via Dockerfile (Playwright / Puppeteer base images).

mysql-app.recommended_path: Railway provides a managed MySQL add-on. Connect via the `${{ MySQL.DATABASE_URL }}` reference.
caveats: Backups: Railway has no managed snapshot — schedule logical dumps to R2/S3.

postgres-app.recommended_path: Railway's Postgres add-on is the canonical path. Reference via `${{ Postgres.DATABASE_URL }}`.
caveats: Backups: schedule pg_dump to R2/S3.
PgBouncer is not deployed by default — install via add-on or Dockerfile if you need it.

mongodb-app.recommended_path: Railway has a community MongoDB template, but for production prefer MongoDB Atlas with a cross-region connection — Railway is not a managed Mongo provider.

redis-app.recommended_path: Railway's Redis add-on is fine for caching and queues. Reference via `${{ Redis.REDIS_URL }}`.
caveats: Persistence config: confirm RDB/AOF settings match your durability needs.

websocket-heavy.recommended_path: Railway runs long-lived processes — WebSockets just work. Scale via numReplicas + sticky session at the client (or Redis pub-sub fanout).
caveats: Public TCP proxy is NOT for WebSockets — use the standard HTTPS domain (wss://) which terminates TLS at Railway's edge.
